establish. Use [] for error_types when the comment is reliable.

pages.text: Our work did not inspect if abstraction-aware models could beneﬁt more from noise-free (golden) labels. In order to make our method easily reproducible we relied on off-the-shelve NLP toolikt predictions, but one direction that could be explored next is to see what happens when abstraction labels come from a ﬁne-tuned model or even from human annotations. 8 In the dec-loss experiments, we did not explore other loss combination strategies: we manually set the overall loss as 0 . 5 l 1 + 0 . 5 l 2 with l 1 and l 2 being the two cross entropy losses we described in Section 3.3. A more sophisticated learning schedule may achieve better performance. Some future exploration could include starting with a heavy weight on learning the abstracted sentence, then slowly decreasing that weight to focus more on the prediction of the target sequence. Previous work showed that pre-trained language models can have some undesired societal biases (Henderson et al., 2018; Shwartz et al., 2020; Bender et al., 2021). Although not explored in this work, we believe that giving abstract entity types like we do in this work could have a positive societal impact on language models, potentially alleviating some of these biases. For instance, through abstraction, a model can be exposed to both female and male names both being “PERSON”s and that a “PERSON” can equally be a “ manager ” or an “ assistant ” regardless of its gender. Similar exposure could be achieved with other abstraction types such as “RELIGION”, “JOB”, “COUNTRY”, “NATIONALITY”, etc... One potential future direction for this work could be to measure the impact explicit abstraction can have on benchmarks such as StereoSet (Nadeem et al., 2020). One hypothesis that results from our work is the following question: could pre-training Transformer models with additional abstraction data result in stronger performance when ﬁne-tuned with abstrac- tion data like we do in this work? Although we could not train from-scratch a T5 model on its original C4 dataset (Raffel et al., 2020), we believe that augmenting C4 with abstract annotations like we do on a smaller scale and training T5 from scratch on this augmented dataset could potentially yield a stronger language model.

arguments.reason: Compare the claim of end-to-end-only results with the paper's reported analyses and caveats.

evidence.quote: In addition, abstraction-aware models showed improved compositional generalization in both interpolation and extrapolation settings.

Our results suggest that the beneﬁts of explicit abstraction could be very signiﬁcant in formally deﬁned logical reasoning settings such as CLUTRR, but point to the notion that explicit abstraction is likely less beneﬁcial for NLP tasks having less formal logical structure.
Our work did not inspect if abstraction-aware models could beneﬁt more from noise-free (golden) labels.

review.explanation: The criticism that the paper does not deeply establish why gains are limited on the natural-language tasks is substantially supported: the paper says it did not test whether noise-free labels would help. But the assertion that it only shows end-to-end performance is too broad. It also reports compositional-generalization results in interpolation and extrapolation and offers an interpretation that abstraction may be less beneficial when tasks have less formal logical structure. The comment overlooks those analyses and discussion.
